did_you_know.text: Did you know? Among the warriors who joined David at Ziklag were archers from Benjamin, described as skilled with both their right and left hands, using both stones and arrows.
Did you know? The men of Gad crossed the Jordan in the first month, when the river was overflowing, and drove away the inhabitants of the valleys to the east and west.
Did you know? When David feared that those coming to him might not be loyal, Amasai, chief of the Thirty, declared, “We are yours, David ... peace,” emphasizing that God was helping David.
Did you know? Men from Manasseh joined David after the Philistine commanders sent him back from the campaign against Saul, fearing that he might betray them and switch sides to Saul.
Did you know? The text says that men came to David day after day to help him, until his camp became very large, “like the camp of God.”
Did you know? The men of Issachar were known not only as warriors, but also as men who understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do; their leaders numbered two hundred.
Did you know? The men of Zebulun supplied fifty thousand warriors, and the text emphasizes that they went to war wholeheartedly, not with divided loyalties.
Did you know? The tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, who lived east of the Jordan, sent a combined force of 120,000 warriors equipped with every kind of weapon.
Did you know? All the forces that gathered at Hebron came wholeheartedly to make David king over all Israel, and the text adds that the rest of Israel were also united in this decision.
Did you know? The coronation celebrations at Hebron lasted three days, and the neighboring tribes brought abundant food on donkeys, camels, mules, and cattle—“because there was joy in Israel.”
